P01 — Counterevidence: The original geometric columns and local sphere-bundle class have independent characteristic-class meaning. Full external bordism generation and surgery are dependencies; at minimum the original lattice, simplification and theorem cannot simultaneously hold. The quadric test survives and no wholesale table rejection is warranted.

P02 — Counterevidence: This affects a principal presentation, not necessarily the separately tested abstract spin table. Possible local coordinate sign changes from P03 do not remove the quintic parity contradiction.
P03 — Counterevidence: The evidence disproves the given relative-class calculation; it does not by itself disprove every final twist theorem or certify corrected attaching/framing geometry.
P04 — Counterevidence: The correction vanishes in the downstream modulo8 quotient, so that generation argument is not refuted; the s3 sign also vanishes modulo2.
P05 — Counterevidence: No high-genus nonsplitting counterexample follows.

P06 — Counterevidence: The subsequent naturality factors the entire integral d2 through H_Gamma=0 and therefore kills torsion as well. Rational rank and the asserted edge surjectivity are not disproved.

proposition.claim:
The standing class consists of smooth, oriented, closed, simply connected six-manifolds \(M\) with \(H_2(M;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z\), a chosen generator \(x\in H^2(M;\mathbb Z)\), and \(d=\langle x^3,[M]\rangle>0\). Write \(x^2=dy\), with \(y\) the corresponding generator of \(H^4(M;\mathbb Z)\), and \(H=H^3(M;\mathbb Z)\), a free symplectic lattice of rank \(2g=b_3(M)\). In the spin case, \[p_1(TM)=4ky,\qquad k=d+6l.\] In the nonspin case, \[d=2\delta,\qquad p_1(TM)=(4k-d)y=(d+48l)y,\qquad
 k=\delta+12l.\] Here \(l\in\mathbb Z\). The Torelli group \(\mathcal I(M)\) is the kernel of the action on \(H\). The variation takes values in \[L_{d,k}=(H\oplus H)/\Delta_{d,k},\qquad
 \Delta_{d,k}=\{(du,ku):u\in H\},\] and \(\mathcal K(M)\) is its kernel. The special Torelli group \(\mathcal J(M)\) acts trivially on \(\pi_3(M)\) and fits into \(1\to\mathcal K(M)\to\mathcal J(M)\to H\to0\). A fixed disk gives the relative group \(\mathcal K(M,D)\).

Normal and tangent Pontryagin classes are distinguished throughout. In particular, for a spin bordism, \(p_1(\nu W)=-p_1(TW)\). The relative characteristic numbers require actual preimages of the specified absolute classes. Replacing such a preimage by a class with different absolute evaluations is not an allowable choice ambiguity.

Theorem6.1 gives K=Z/3; the claimed original relation lattice and generator image give order21.
